final_selections.research_reason: Team A's shots on target production at home is substantially above its own overall long-run average, driven by a strong home possession and final-third-entry profile. The venue-conditioned baseline isolates whether the home environment is a systematic driver rather than noise.
final_selections.mechanism_summary: High home possession (raw_rows) enables sustained attacking phases, translating to elevated final-third entries at home. More sustained pressure in the final third converts into a higher rate of shots on target at home than away, creating a genuine venue-conditioned production uplift above the undifferentiated long-run mean.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: Team A's home and away SoT production differ materially (raw_rows). A simple average blends these two distinct environments and would understate the home-specific elevation. The venue-conditioned comparator isolates this structural split.
final_selections.support_warning: Both home and away sample sizes are adequate (n=12/13), but home/away imbalance means venue-conditioned estimates may carry moderate variance.

final_selections.research_reason: Team A's corner production at home is dramatically higher than away (raw_rows), with the home mean substantially above both the long-run mean and the league environment. The venue-conditioned test evaluates whether this home corner elevation is a persistent structural feature.
final_selections.mechanism_summary: Team A's high home possession and extensive final-third entries (raw_rows) create more sustained attacking pressure near the opposition box, leading to more corners via blocked shots and clearances off the line. Away from home, possession and pressure drop, so corners generated also drop — this is a venue-driven structural mechanism, not randomness.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: The home/away split for Team A corners is among the largest in the data (raw_rows). The long-run mean averages two very different distributions; the venue-conditioned comparator correctly isolates the home component.
final_selections.support_warning: Corner production can be volatile match to match even when the underlying structural tendency is real.

This hypothesis tests whether Team A's SoT production is further elevated when the opponent is in the HIGH goals_against tercile — a direct opponent-dependent conditional structure, not just a venue average.
final_selections.mechanism_summary: A HIGH goals_against opponent (Team B) is susceptible to conceding because of structural defensive weakness away (raw_rows: above-league shots/SoT against, above-league goals against). Against such opponents, Team A's already-elevated home attack is likely to generate more shots on target than its venue-only average. The condition creates a genuine opponent-quality filter rather than a blind average.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: The unconditional venue baseline includes games against well-organized defenses. Conditioning on opponents with HIGH goals_against profiles isolates a more vulnerable defensive cohort that matches Team B's actual profile, making the comparison more information-rich.
final_selections.support_warning: The opponent_profile condition uses similar-opponent cohort membership; cohort size not explicitly reported here, so conditional sample size may be smaller.

final_selections.research_reason: Team B's shots_against profile is HIGH (opponent_profile from Team A's view). This hypothesis conditions Team A's corner production on opponents with HIGH shots_against profiles — teams that absorb a lot of offensive pressure and consequently concede more corners. Team B shows HIGH shots_against and also concedes a high corner rate away (raw_rows).
final_selections.mechanism_summary: Teams that face HIGH shots_against are structurally besieged, which means attackers generate many blocked/deflected shots and clearances that result in corners. Team A pressing deeply into Team B's defensive block creates repeated corner-generating situations. Conditioning corners FOR on HIGH shots_against opponents isolates this mechanism specifically.
final_selections.why_simple_average_is_insufficient: Teams that allow high shot volumes necessarily create more corner-generating defensive situations than the average opponent. Blending all opponent types obscures this mechanism; the opponent-profile condition activates the structural link between opponent defensive fragility and corner generation.
final_selections.support_warning: Corner counts have high match-to-match variance; single-game realization may deviate significantly even when the structural tendency is well-supported.
